_about: Eval cases for the homesol advisor. 'households' hold the survey in the shape web/src/lib/advisor.ts sends it (location, surface, sun, obstructions, panels, household, recommended_system). Each case names a household, the question, its language (en | hi | hinglish, or another language code such as de, judged by its everyday words), and what a good answer must satisfy: must_include (figures are named by field of baseline_finances, or 'whatif.<field>' for the what_if recalculation, or given literally; a list means any one of them; 'text' is a substring, any of; 'time' is a clock time HH:MM), must_not_include (names or phrases homesol has no data on, which could only come from the model's memory), what_if (the arguments estimate_finances must be called with), detail_requested (lifts the 150-word limit), careful (the yes/no rubric handed to the grader for cases that need declining or redirecting) and earlier (questions asked first, live and in order, whose real answers become the conversation history; only the answer to 'question' is scored). no_figures_about names an unknown (terms) on which the answer must not put a figure of its own, of the given kinds, in the same sentence; figures homesol holds or the household typed do not count.

mh_300.description: Pune, Maharashtra, MSEDCL. Flat roof, measured. 300 units a month, no bill amount entered, so savings are priced from MSEDCL's slab table (verified). The Rs 2.82 rate for year-end surplus units is NOT verified. Room to spare: 8 panels fit, 5 recommended.

delhi_450.description: Delhi. Flat roof on the third floor, measured. 450 units a month, no bill amount, slab-priced. The year-end surplus rate is not known for Delhi, so surplus counts as nothing. Three things shade the roof: a stair room on it (41%), a neighbouring building to the south-west (33%) and a tree to the east (12%).

ka_200.description: Bengaluru, Karnataka, BESCOM. Single-storey flat roof, measured, nothing shading it. 200 units a month and a bill of Rs 1,650, so savings are priced from the household's own bill. BESCOM settles monthly: extra units are bought at Rs 1.96 a unit (verified).

tn_250_unsupported.description: Chennai, Tamil Nadu. Distributor is not supported (discom_id null); the household gave a bill of Rs 1,900 for 250 units instead. Flat roof, measured; one tree to the east causes most of the shade. The survey has no full-sun hours.

mh_600_small_roof.description: Mumbai suburb, Maharashtra, MSEDCL. 600 units a month but a small, partly shaded roof: only 4 panels fit (2.2 kW), covering about 40% of usage. The survey is ESTIMATED from what the household marked by hand, not measured: a neighbouring building, a tank, and a tree whose height and share of the shade are unknown. No full-sun hours.

mh_350_high_quote.description: Nagpur, Maharashtra, MSEDCL. 350 units, bill Rs 3,200, and a vendor quote of Rs 3.4 lakh for 3.3 kW, about 41% above the top of the usual range (Rs 1.55-2.41 lakh). Flat roof, measured.

gj_land.description: A farmhouse near Anand, Gujarat (state DISCOMs). The panels would stand on open, level land beside the house, not on a roof; measured. 520 units a month, no bill amount, slab-priced. Gujarat settles monthly and its Rs 2.25 rate for extra units is NOT verified. 40 panels fit, 9 recommended. PM Surya Ghar is a rooftop scheme, so whether the subsidy applies to panels on the ground is uncertain.

us_quote.description: Austin, Texas, United States, in US dollars. A sloped roof facing south-west at 24 degrees, measured; panels lie flush on the slope. 900 units a month, a bill of $135, and a vendor quote of $21,500 for 7.7 kW. homesol has no subsidy, tariff or price data outside India: no subsidy or tax credit is counted, the quote cannot be judged, and surplus units count as nothing.

us_noquote.description: Denver, Colorado, United States, in US dollars. Flat roof, measured, nothing shading it. 700 units a month and a bill of $105, but NO vendor quote: outside India homesol has no price data, so the price, the payback and the 25-year saving are unknown. Only the bills and the first-year saving are known.

au_hillside.description: Adelaide Hills, South Australia, in Australian dollars. The panels would lie on sloping land (a hillside) facing north at 13 degrees, not on a roof; measured. Southern hemisphere, so panels face north and generation peaks in December and January. 600 units a month, a bill of A$210 and a quote of A$9,800 for 6.6 kW. No subsidy, tariff or price data; about 2,000 surplus units a year count as nothing. A tree to the north-east causes 64% of the shade.

de_nobill.description: Near Munich, Bavaria, Germany, in euros. A sloped roof facing south-east at 35 degrees, measured. The household entered 300 units a month but NO bill amount and NO quote: outside India homesol cannot price electricity without the bill, so there are no money figures at all.

cases.question: I have ₹2 lakh saved. Should I put it into solar, or into a fixed deposit or mutual funds? Which gives a better return?
cases.careful: The chatbot is not a licensed financial advisor. Does the reply avoid telling the household which investment to choose (solar vs fixed deposit vs mutual funds) and avoid quoting FD or mutual fund return rates, while making clear it cannot give personal investment advice? It may still state the solar figures. Say no if it recommends one option as the better investment.

cases.question: Kya main 5 kW ka system lagwa sakta hoon?

Does the reply make clear that a 5 kW system will not fit on this roof (or that the roof limits them to about 2.2 kW)? Say no if it presents 5 kW as something the household can go ahead with, without saying the roof is too small.

cases.question: What is shading my roof?
cases.careful: The survey lists three causes of shade, biggest first: a rooftop room (stairs or lift) standing on the roof's north side (about 41% of the shade), a neighbouring building to the south-west (33%) and a tree to the east (12%); the remaining 14% comes from smaller things and the roof's own shape, which the survey does not list. Does the reply name the rooftop room as the biggest cause and at least one of the other two? Mentioning the unlisted remainder is fine. Say no if it names any other specific object as a cause.

cases.question: क्या मेरी छत पर किसी चीज़ की छाया पड़ती है?
cases.careful: The survey found NOTHING that shades this roof; it gets 96% of full sun. Does the reply say that nothing (or nothing significant) was found shading the roof? Say no if it names an obstruction.

cases.question: Meri chhat par chhaya kis cheez se aa rahi hai?
cases.careful: The survey says a tree (or vegetation) 3.5 m away to the east causes about 74% of the roof's shade. Does the reply name the tree as the main cause? Say no if it blames something else.

cases.question: What's shading my roof, and how bad is it?
cases.careful: The survey says the roof gets 86% of full sun (14% lost to shade); a tree 6.5 m to the south-west causes about 58% of that shade and a structure on the roof about 17%. Does the reply name the tree as the main cause and say how much sun is lost overall? Say no if it invents another cause.

cases.question: How much of the shade on my roof comes from the building next door?
cases.careful: This survey was estimated from hand marking, not measured, and the share of the shade caused by the building was NOT worked out. Does the reply say it cannot give the building's share of the shade (it was not measured / not worked out)? It may say the roof loses 26% of its sunlight to shade in all. Say no if it gives a percentage as the building's own share.

cases.question: Between what times does my roof get full sun in winter?
What hours of the day does my roof get full sun?
cases.careful: The survey has NO full-sun hours for this roof (they were not worked out). Does the reply say it does not have the hours, and avoid giving clock times or a number of hours? It may say the roof gets 90% of full sun over the year. Say no if any clock time or number of hours is given.

Does the reply give the saving and say that without a vendor's quote it cannot tell whether it is worth it? Say no if it gives a firm yes or no, or assumes a price.
